main_text.p: verf. 37. Luc. 14. v. 26. 1. Reg. 2. v. 19. & seqq. Obseruantia est, quâ liberi animum suum honorificum erga parentes aliis etiam declarant: puta comitate in verbis; industria in suscipiendis & peti ficiendis iis, quæ parentib. sciunt honori esse & delectationi; ministeriis denique & officiosi-tate. Leuit. 19. v. 3. Deut. 27. v. 16. Ecclesiastic. 3. v. 2. & seqq. Tob. 4. v. 3. & seqq. Huius obseruantiæ pars magna est regere, & quasi condonare infirmitates parentum, præsertim vbi confenuerunt. Gen. 9. verf. 23. Prou. 20. v. 20. c. 23. ver. 22. c. 30. v. 17. Eccles. 3. v. 13. 14. 15. Gratitudo est, quâ liberi parentes senio confectos, si necessitas postulat, victum alunt ac iuuant, quod Græci eleganter dicunt 5ἀντιπελαργεῖν[?]. Gen. 47. v. 1. & seqq. 1. Tim. 5. v. 4. Eccles. 3. v. 15. 16. 17.
XXII. Officium liberorum erga se inuicem consistit in mutuo amore & auxilio. Vide Psal. 133. Gen. 37.

XXIII. Officium in societate herili est dominorum erga seruos, seruorum erga dominos, & seruorum erga se inuicem. Officium dominorum erga seruos est directio seruorum ad exercitia pietatis, & operas vitæ necessarias. Directio ad exercitia pietatis in primis in eo vertitur, vt heri hoc agant vt serui audiant conciones, & sabbatum recte transigant. Exod. 20. v. 10. 1. Sam. 1. v. 21. Ioh. 4. ver. 53. Act. 10. v. 2. Directio ad operas est, qua pater & materfamilias exigunt a seruis pensum ordinarium. Eccles. 33. v. 28. 29. & laborantibus dant competentem cibum & potum iusto tempore. 1. Tim. 5. verf. 18. Matth. 24. v. 45. Eccles. 33. v. 25. & numerant mercedem debitam. Leuit. 19. v. 13. Deut. 24. v. 14. Luc. 10. v. 7. & tuentur seruos contra iniuriam aliorum. Eccles. 33. v. 31. item sequuntur-proprium consilia bona. Eccles. 10. v. 28. fidelitatem quoq; ipsorum compensant præmiis, procuratione coniugij, curatione valetudinis aduersæ &c. Matth. 25. v. 21. Ecclesiastic. 7. v. 20. 21. fugiunt insuper indulgentiam in seruos,

page.notes: Marginal numbers (5, 10, 15, 20) stand along the right margin, probably line or section markers; only the first is placed in the text. The Greek word after "dicunt" is doubtful. The text "sequuntur-proprium" in the XXIII paragraph is a reading of "sequuntur-pforum", which may be a printing error for "proprium", left as printed in spirit. The number "5" beside the XXII line and the "10" and "15" beside later lines are not separately placed because the scan is faint there. The catchword "& fa-" is the first word of the next page.
